# Contract Reconstruction — Isolated Session Download + Isolation Stickiness

## 1. R Table

### 1.1 Settled (directly supplied)

| ID | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Isolated session's download command must reliably complete. Today it cannot; default-session download works. | reported defect |
| R2 | Isolated download completes in that session's chosen destination. | specified, user acceptance |
| R3 | Satisfying R2 must not reconfigure the default session's or any other session's download destination. | specified, user acceptance |
| R4 | An invalid isolation request must not change effective isolation behavior of later flagless commands. | reported defect |
| R5 | An invalid isolation request must introduce no new sticky state. | reported defect |
| R6 | Failed connections likewise cannot newly enable or contaminate sticky isolation — in memory and across daemon restart. | specified |
| R7 | A compatible, successful isolated connection must persist isolation across flag omission and across reconnect. | specified |
| R8 | Prior successful isolation remains the standing intent after a later request fails (failure does not demote). | existing session contract |
| R9 | Reconnect/reuse preserves context, bound target, URL, storage, ordinary continuity while browser/context is alive. | existing session contract |
| R10 | A dead browser may legitimately require replacement context + state restoration (continuity relaxed, not intent). | existing session contract |
| R11 | Explicit close clears isolation state and binding; a subsequent new session may start non-isolated. | explicit-close contract |
| R12 | false or omitted isolation field is not an explicit clear of persisted intent. | explicit-close contract |
| R13 | Launch envelope and later action envelope are separate requests; a later action failure does not roll back a completed launch. | command protocol |
| R14 | Within one request, success is not final while mandatory post-processing can still fail. | command protocol |
| R15 | Isolation partitions cooperative sessions only; not controllers holding global CDP authority. | scope |
| R16 | No crash-atomicity or strict remote cleanup guarantee once transport/host is unavailable. | scope |
| R17 | Even under R16, a failed request must not publish successful isolation, and existing sessions must not be corrupted. | scope |
| R18 | Must-not-change set (see §5). | specified |

### 1.2 Derived (labelled inference, not new contract)

| ID | Derived requirement | Derivation |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Isolation intent is per-session persisted state, distinct from per-command flag input. | R7 + R12 + R11 |
| D2 | Publication of isolation intent must be gated on the whole request succeeding, including mandatory post-processing. | R5 + R6 + R14 + R17 |
| D3 | Therefore intent-publication has a commit point; validation-failure and connect-failure both precede it. | D2 |
| D4 | Persisted intent must survive daemon restart when, and only when, it was validly published. | R6 (restart-scoped) + R7 (reconnect-scoped) |
| D5 | Download destination is a per-session attribute, not a browser-global one, at least for isolated sessions. | R2 + R3 |
| D6 | Download completion is an observable terminal condition, not merely "command accepted". | R1 wording "reliably complete" + R14 |
| D7 | Two failure classes must be distinguishable: invalid request (rejected before any effect) and failed connection (attempted, no effect published). Both share the same no-sticky-state outcome. | R4/R5 vs R6 |
| D8 | State machine must tolerate the launch-success/action-failure split without demoting intent established by the launch. | R13 + R8 |
| D9 | A dead-browser recovery path re-establishes isolation from persisted intent rather than requiring the flag again. | R7 + R10 |
| D10 | Sessions must not observe each other's download configuration changes; cross-session write is a defect even if it makes R1 pass. | R3 |

### 1.3 Undecided (materially blocking, must be resolved by source/runtime probe)

| ID | Open question | Why it blocks shape |
|---|---|---|
| U1 | Which attach/post-processing stages are fallible, and where the current implicit commit point sits. | Determines where D3's gate can legally live. |
| U2 | Whether download destination is currently browser-global, target-global, or context-scoped on the supported substrate(s). | Determines whether R2+R3 are simultaneously satisfiable without a new mechanism. |
| U3 | Whether the persisted-intent store is written before or after connection validation, and its restart-durability semantics. | Determines whether R6 is currently violated at rest or only in memory. |
| U4 | Download-completion signal availability per substrate (event-based vs filesystem observation). | Determines the observable in S3/S4 below. |
| U5 | Whether "compatible external connection" compatibility is checked pre- or post-publication. | Distinguishes invalid-request from failed-connection ordering. |

Non-blocking unknowns (deferred): exact propagation routes, transport/filesystem cleanup behavior, cross-session event delivery.

## 2. Temporal State Transitions

States: N no persisted intent · P isolated intent persisted (published) · A intent persisted and live isolated context bound · X closed/cleared.

| # | From | Event | To | Observable obligation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | N | flagless command | N | Non-isolated behavior. |
| T2 | N | isolation request, invalid | N | Rejected; no in-memory or on-disk delta (R4, R5). |
| T3 | N | isolation request valid, connection fails | N | Error surfaced; nothing published (R6, R17). |
| T4 | N | isolation request valid, connect + mandatory post-processing succeed | A | Intent published exactly once at commit (D2). |
| T5 | A | flagless command | A | Isolation still applied (R7). |
| T6 | A | isolate=false or field omitted | A | Not a clear (R12). |
| T7 | A | later request fails (any class) | A | Intent retained; no demotion (R8). |
| T8 | A | reconnect / reuse, browser alive | A | Context, bound target, URL, storage preserved (R9). |
| T9 | A | browser dead → reconnect | A' | Replacement context permitted; state restored; intent unchanged (R10, D9). |
| T10 | A / P | daemon restart | P → A on next use | Valid intent survives restart (R6 inverse, R7). |
| T11 | N | daemon restart after T2/T3 | N | No intent materialized post-restart (R6). |
| T12 | A | explicit close | X→N | Isolation state and binding cleared; next new session may be non-isolated (R11). |
| T13 | A | launch envelope OK, later action envelope fails | A | No rollback of launch (R13). |
| T14 | A | download command | A | Completes in session destination; other sessions' destinations unchanged (R1, R2, R3). |

## 3. Observable Success Criteria

- S1 Isolated session issues download → command reaches a terminal completed state, not hang/timeout/indefinite-pending (R1, D6).
- S2 Downloaded artifact lands in the isolated session's chosen destination (R2).
- S3 Default session's and any third session's download destination readback is byte-identical before/after S1–S2 (R3, D10).
- S4 Default-session download continues to work unchanged after the isolated flow (regression guard).
- S5 Invalid isolation request → error; immediately following flagless command behaves exactly as it would have before the invalid request (R4).
- S6 After invalid request or failed connection, daemon restart yields non-isolated flagless behavior (R5, R6).
- S7 After one successful isolated connection, flagless commands stay isolated; after reconnect, still isolated; after daemon restart, still isolated (R7).
- S8 After success then a subsequent failure, flagless behavior remains isolated (R8).
- S9 Reconnect with live browser preserves bound target, current URL, storage (R9).
- S10 Explicit close, then new session with no flag → non-isolated (R11); isolate=false alone → still isolated (R12).
- S11 Concurrent sessions: no session observes another's isolation or download-destination mutation (R15, D10).

## 4. Ownership / Lifecycle / Authority

- Session owns: its isolation intent record, its bound context/target, its download destination (D5), its persisted-intent durability.
- Daemon owns: session registry, restart-time rehydration of published intents only, the commit point that publishes intent (D3).
- Browser/external connection owns: context lifetime; may die independently → R10 relaxation.
- Authority boundary: isolation is cooperative-session partitioning; a controller holding global CDP authority is out of scope and may bypass partitioning (R15). No guarantee is offered against it.
- Failure-domain boundary: once transport/host is unavailable, cleanup is best-effort (R16), but publication and neighbor-integrity invariants still hold (R17).

## 5. Must-Not-Change Set

Pinned-session binding; compatible reconnect and restart behavior; user-defined environment configuration; browser-owned vs externally-connected modes; recording of the current page; the default session's download path; existing envelope/wire formats; existing public flags (no new ones); unrelated features; no published/released surface changes.

## 6. Discriminator Matrix

Cases where superficially conforming implementations diverge:

| # | Scenario | Conforming outcome | Divergent-but-plausible outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| K1 | Isolated download while default session idle | Default destination untouched | Global destination mutated to satisfy R2 (violates R3) |
| K2 | Isolated download, then default download | Both land in own destinations | Default inherits isolated path (R3) |
| K3 | Invalid isolation request, then flagless | Non-isolated | Isolated, because intent was written before validation (R4/R5) |
| K4 | Valid request, connection fails, then restart | Non-isolated | Isolated, intent persisted pre-connect (R6, U3) |
| K5 | Success, then later failure | Still isolated | Demoted to non-isolated (R8) |
| K6 | isolate=false after success | Still isolated | Cleared (R12) |
| K7 | Explicit close, then new session | Non-isolated | Still isolated from stale record (R11) |
| K8 | Launch OK, action fails | Launch effects retained | Launch rolled back (R13) |
| K9 | Connect OK, mandatory post-processing fails | Treated as failed; nothing published | Published on connect-success (R14, D2) |
| K10 | Browser dead, reconnect | New context, intent preserved, state restored | Intent lost with context (R10, D9) |
| K11 | Global-CDP controller present | No guarantee claimed | Implementation claims partitioning it cannot enforce (R15) |
| K12 | Host/transport gone mid-request | Best-effort cleanup, no publication, neighbors intact | Neighbor session corrupted or partial publication (R16, R17) |
| K13 | Download "accepted" vs "completed" | Terminal completion observed | Success returned at initiation (D6, U4) |

Blocking unknowns before shaping: U1–U5.
